newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Jan 21 - CPO production in December fell 16.4 percent or 124,700 tonnes to 637,900 tonnes. As expected production in Peninsular Malaysia shrank 17.6 percent while East Malaysia posted a smaller decline of 12.8 percent. For the whole year production expanded 7.4 percent or 575,200 tonnes to 8.386 million tonnes. Peninsular Malaysia accounted for 54.4 percent of the increase when its output rose 5.1 percent to 6.407 million tonnes. East Malaysia posted another year of robust growth when its production expanded 15.3 percent or 262,500 tonnes to 1.978 million tonnes.

The commendable expansion in CPO production of 575,200 tonnes in 1996 was matched by equally impressive growth in offtake as reflected in a drawdown in stocks of palm oil to 792,700 tonnes at end December from 859,900 tonnes at the start of the year. Compared to November, stocks fell a hefty 163,300 tonnes. Stocks of CPO alone fell 168,500 tonnes to 435,400 tonnes at end December. The level was much lower then our estimate because we did not expect refiners to convert so much of their CPO and held them in the form of PPO stocks.

In the last several months when both production and offtake were large we managed to come out with estimate on CPO production and palm oil stocks that closely matched official figures released by PORLA. From the regular field crop surveys conducted we also attempted to provide as reliable projections on production as possible. We do not engage in plagiarism as some including brokers and those in the wire service had done We won't engage in armchair forcasting nor do we rely on hearsays. You can't be ethical and professional if you refuse to acknowledge the sources or fail to obtain authorision for the data presented in your reports.

Above all, we have no respect for subscribers who promptly fax our reports to third parties. Non- subscribers who in turn circulate reports to their clients deserve nothing but contempt. This is piracy. We apologise for the above digression. In the last two weeks Sabah and Sarawak had been hit by a resumption of monsoon rains. Tentatively we estimate CPO production in January to deline 9 percent. If the rains are prolonged a double-digit decline could not be ruled out. Should there be high FFA/M+I problems as well, it would aggravate the increasingly tight CPO supplies situation.

Palm oil exports are expected to drop considerably to 545,000 tonnes in January from 638,000 tonnes (Porla Figure)- 675,000 tonnes in December and our December 20 projection of 560,000-565,000 tonnes. As offtake still exceeds production, palm oil stocks would be further reduced to an estimated 730,000 tonnes and end January from 775,000 tonnes projected a month ago. March CPO futures had retreaded 34 ringgit to 1,266 ringgit yesterday from 1,300 ringgit on January 13 - highest in 12 months. We view the pullback as healthy.
It would pave the way for a strong recovery in exports from March onward. The reduction from 18% to 12% in import duty on PPO by China this month also augurs well for the commodity this year.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
